CandidateGap.description:
Describe one critical or possibly critical coverage gap.

Parameters
----------
gap_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
gap_status : Literal["critical", "possible"]
    Strength of the model's gap assessment.
missing_metadata_concept : str
    Reusable snapshot metadata that may not be adequately covered.
proposed_field_name : str
    Suggested snake-case label for human review, not an accepted field.
evidence : str
    Concise evidence from the supplied snapshot and document context.
why_snapshot_metadata : str
    Reason the concept describes the snapshot rather than only its document.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1.1 fields that most closely represent the concept.
why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient : str
    Possible semantic loss when using the closest existing fields.
material_impact : Literal["interpretability", "discoverability", "both"]
    Area materially affected if the information is not covered.
material_consequence : str
    Concrete impairment caused by omission or inadequate representation.
uncertainty_note : str | None
    Remaining evidential or materiality uncertainty, if any.

content.text: {"coverage_assessment":"possible_gap","critical_or_possible_gaps":[{"gap_id":"gap_1","gap_status":"possible","missing_metadata_concept":"Structured associations between components of a composite snapshot and their respective titles, visualization types, variables, time periods, and measurement contexts.","proposed_field_name":"component_metadata_relationships","evidence":"The snapshot is a composite page with multiple visible components: tables headed “POVERTY and SOCIAL,” “KEY ECONOMIC RATIOS and LONG-TERM TRENDS,” and “STRUCTURE of the ECONOMY,” plus separate charts titled “Development diamond*,” “Economic ratios*,” “Growth of investment and GDP (%),” and “Growth of exports and imports (%).” These components use different variables, time periods, units, and comparison groups.","why_snapshot_metadata":"The component titles, chart/table forms, and their associated indicators and time contexts are visible within the snapshot itself and describe the organization and meaning of this specific analytical object, not merely the parent document.","closest_schema_fields":["visualization_type","panel_title","variable_name","time_period","unit_of_measure","measure_type","comparison_group","row_dimension","column_dimension","category_dimension"],"why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient":"The closest fields can record a flat list of panel titles, variables, periods, units, and an overall composite visualization type, but they do not preserve which variable, unit, time period, or comparison group belongs to which table or chart component. For this snapshot, flattening may mix contexts from several distinct panels and charts.","material_impact":"interpretability","material_consequence":"A metadata record could indicate that the snapshot contains many indicators, years, units, and chart types, but not whether a given indicator is part of a table, radar-style comparison chart, or line chart, making the summarized metadata ambiguous for interpreting the composite figure without re-examining the image.","uncertainty_note":"The materiality is uncertain because v1.1.1 explicitly allows composite snapshots to be summarized at the overall level and defers component-to-type normalization; if detailed component extraction is handled outside the snapshot metadata schema, the impairment may be reduced."}]}

critical_or_possible_gaps.missing_metadata_concept: Structured associations between components of a composite snapshot and their respective titles, visualization types, variables, time periods, and measurement contexts.
critical_or_possible_gaps.evidence: The snapshot is a composite page with multiple visible components: tables headed “POVERTY and SOCIAL,” “KEY ECONOMIC RATIOS and LONG-TERM TRENDS,” and “STRUCTURE of the ECONOMY,” plus separate charts titled “Development diamond*,” “Economic ratios*,” “Growth of investment and GDP (%),” and “Growth of exports and imports (%).” These components use different variables, time periods, units, and comparison groups.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_snapshot_metadata: The component titles, chart/table forms, and their associated indicators and time contexts are visible within the snapshot itself and describe the organization and meaning of this specific analytical object, not merely the parent document.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient: The closest fields can record a flat list of panel titles, variables, periods, units, and an overall composite visualization type, but they do not preserve which variable, unit, time period, or comparison group belongs to which table or chart component. For this snapshot, flattening may mix contexts from several distinct panels and charts.
critical_or_possible_gaps.material_consequence: A metadata record could indicate that the snapshot contains many indicators, years, units, and chart types, but not whether a given indicator is part of a table, radar-style comparison chart, or line chart, making the summarized metadata ambiguous for interpreting the composite figure without re-examining the image.
critical_or_possible_gaps.uncertainty_note: The materiality is uncertain because v1.1.1 explicitly allows composite snapshots to be summarized at the overall level and defers component-to-type normalization; if detailed component extraction is handled outside the snapshot metadata schema, the impairment may be reduced.
